findings.title: Heldout validation is conditional on the frozen graph
findings.detail: Curvature screening, piece membership/degrees and nominated-family grouping were determined from the complete frozen graph. Their selection is not retrained inside folds. The protocol already discloses this, so claims should remain a conditional noise-law comparison rather than independent pipeline/noise-truth validation.

findings.title: Whole-family holdouts do not establish time-block transfer
findings.detail: The seeded folds group nominated families and unmatched tracks, not time blocks. Shared receiver disturbances can span held families at the same times; unknown shared emitters can also be undergrouped. This is not a flaw in the stated family-only protocol, but the result should not be presented as randomized time-block or temporal-transfer validation.

findings.title: Training noise fit is a plug-in surrogate
findings.detail: Leverage-corrected residual squares are correlated and mix neighboring variances under heteroscedasticity. The inherited fit_variance optimizer profiles an unclipped law, while learn/variance score and apply its clipped version. Thus the training BIC quantity is a selection heuristic, not an exact likelihood/BIC for independent raw errors. The heldout full-contrast covariance and its determinant are algebraically correct and protect the stated model comparison.

findings.title: Predictive-point noise transfer is not separately validated
findings.detail: Noise laws are estimated and cross-validated on curved graph pieces, then applied by receiver/margin to predictive-only points as well. This matches the inherited plug-in architecture but does not independently establish those points' true frequency-error variance.
